thread:
lena: Hey support, customer acme-app (prod) is seeing a sudden shift: most signed requests are landing in eu-west instead of their pinned us-east endpoint. They're getting intermittent 401s and tail latency spikes (300-800ms). Started ~03:10 UTC. Billing also shows a spike in egress to eu-west. Can someone take a look?

mike: Do we have a sample request-id + their policy blob? I can grep logs.

lena: request-id: req_0a7c9f23, api-key: ak_live_XXXXX (sent privately). Paste of policy from console (sanitized):
```json
{"customer_id":"acme","routing": {"model":"text-gen-1","priorityOrder": [], "regions": [{"name":"us-east-1","weight":"100","affinity":"session","ttl":3600},{"name":"eu-west-1","weight":0,"affinity":"none"}]}}
```

anya: quick suspicion — priorityOrder is empty which should be invalid. Our fallback policy code was recently changed to fall back to lexicographic region ordering if priorityOrder is missing/empty. That would make "eu-west-1" win over "us-east-1". Also seeing note about affinity: session cookie not being set for some requests (so sticky routing isn't keeping them in us-east).

infra-oncall: I pulled service logs for req_0a7c9f23: routing decision used fallback path with key: `fallback_order=alpha(region.name)` at 03:10:32. There's also a 401 coming from the eu-west auth-gateway: `token validation failed: session cookie missing`.

mike: Where did priorityOrder become empty? Any recent UI/console migrations?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: frontend-console v2.14.1 -> 2026-03-16T03:05:00Z (commit: 9f4b2d).

anya: That console release included a small change to how we serialize priorityOrder for legacy policies; bug: if region weights all zero except primary, we were normalizing out priorityOrder and writing an empty array. The runtime expects either a non-empty array or the `priority` field on each region. Runtime fallback to alphabetical was an unexpected regression.

lena: That matches timeline. Customer claims they never edited policy. Console migration likely touched their saved policy during rollout.

infra-oncall: Short-term mitigation: we can hotpatch routing to prefer preserved region metadata if affinity cookie exists, and treat empty priorityOrder as 'preserve existing explicit region priorities' instead of alpha fallback. I'll open a hotfix.

mike: Repro steps I used: 1) create legacy policy with single primary region weight 100 and no priorityOrder; 2) run console-migration script against it; 3) observe saved policy `priorityOrder: []` in DB and routing decisions go to eu-west. PR to add to unit tests.

anya: Also need to fix affinity cookie setting — console migration stripped the cookie domain for multi-tenant orgs, so session-affinity wasn't binding for some keys. That's why requests lost sticky pin and hit fallback.

billing: Customer reported a billing jump ~03:12 UTC. Suggest offering credit for cross-region egress + rapid response. I'll prepare a provisional credit and T-shirt.

infra-oncall: Action items: (1) Roll hotfix to routing (treat empty priorityOrder as missing -> use per-region priority) — will push in 10m. (2) Revert migration change in console that normalizes out empty priorityOrder. (3) Fix affinity cookie domain write and backfill affected policies. (4) Add tests for empty-array fallback and cookie behavior.

mike: I'll take (2) + tests. Assigning to me.

lena: I'll coordinate with acme-app and gate the credit with billing.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: routing-hotfix v1.2.3 -> 2026-03-16T03:18:00Z (canary 5%).

infra-oncall: Canary looks clean so far, routing decisions are back to us-east for acme requests, no further 401s on those req ids. Increasing rollout to 50%.

billing: Credit prepared, sending now. Notifying customer.

anya: Postmortem notes: root cause = console migration normalization dropped priorityOrder for certain legacy policies; compounded by affinity cookie domain bug. Two fixes: runtime defensive fallback change + rollback fix and cookie backfill.

lena: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the customer and close after all rollouts/backfills finish. :white_check_mark:
